edits.new:
Choose the broadest coherent interpretation of the selected subject supported by its context, original hierarchy and post, preserving its identity and expressed restrictions. Apply this preference while selecting the category's defining conditions, not only after a meaning has been chosen. When both a category and a restricted subset of it are supported, choose the category. Retain a restriction only when the selected subject expresses it or the evidence establishes it as necessary to identify that topic. Interpretations referring to different things or different word meanings must be resolved from the input; do not combine them to manufacture a larger category. Unknown facts about an instance remain unknown even when a broader category is chosen.

Resolve each ambiguity under this preference.
edits.old: Resolve each ambiguity using the selected subject, its context, the original branch and the post.

edits.new: Preserve the selected topic's identity and expressed restrictions; do not combine competing senses to avoid deciding.
edits.old: Do not substitute a broader or narrower topic or combine competing interpretations to avoid deciding.
